_note: Visual sign-off for phoenix-volumetric-v1.glb, decided by inspecting the matte renders in /tmp/phoenix-qa. Written by hand, not by the pipeline. Anything not genuinely readable in the renders is left false or null.

_caveats.beak: Hooked beak reads in profile, side 3/4 and the head close-up. From the pure front camera it is foreshortened, which is bird anatomy rather than a defect.
_caveats.hero_feather_visual: The outline reads quill-narrow base -> vane belly -> tapered tip, and the lead primary stands clear of the fan. The rachis itself is a thickness ridge: measured at mid-vane it is 0.045 thick on the shaft line against 0.003 at the vane edges, with an asymmetric 0.024 / 0.169 vane split. A matte silhouette seen on the vane cannot show that ridge; it shows in shaded render.
_caveats.no_plate_look: Wing and neck outlines carry a fine serration where the covert row overlaps. Those are the edges of separate solid feathers, not notches cut into a plate.
_caveats.tail_feathers: Five to six plumes separate cleanly in the outline; the inner plumes overlap in projection. The tail is a splayed 3D bundle, not a flat fan.
